expectations_are: rule-derived predictions from manual trace of the design, not outputs of a run

cases.note: A: one local match; 'increased' merges as embedded content of 'found' via the 'that' boundary.

cases.text: Previous studies found that scores increased.
cases.note: B: one local match, still returned -- NOT suppressed for being prior_work. This module never inspects source.

cases.text: Previous studies found X. We found Y.
cases.note: C: two distinct local assertions (separate sentences), never collapsed to one.

cases.text: A review concluded that X is associated with Y.
cases.note: D: 'concluded' is not in the mapper's predicate lexicon at all; 'associated' is the sole match. Preserved and attached locally -- this module does not decide whether review evidence is admissible.

cases.text: We hypothesized X and found Y.
cases.note: E: 'hypothesized' is not in the mapper's predicate lexicon at all, so 'found' is the only match -- the result attaches to the Y assertion, never the hypothesis, by construction (there is no competing predicate span for 'hypothesized' to begin with). content_span is anchored at 'found', excluding the hypothesis clause, even though assertion_span/clause_span remain the whole sentence for context.

cases.text: We found no evidence that scores increased.
cases.note: F: one local match remains representable, not deleted. Whether this is vetoed for authority is a separate, later question (I4-1c's own validation layer, cross-checked in the test file, never read here).
